title: Modern Masters
description: The turn into modernism — symbolism, expression, and the new century (public-domain works).

items.title: Male Nude with Left Foot on a Pedestal
items.medium: Graphite and white heightening on brown wove paper
items.description_narrative: This early drawing by Gustav Klimt, created in 1879, depicts a male nude figure in a classical pose, his left foot resting upon a pedestal. Executed with graphite and white heightening on brown wove paper, it reveals the artist's foundational academic training.
items.tags: male nude, figure study, academic, drawing, figurative, early work, classical

items.title: Male Nude
items.medium: Various graphite pencils, with erasing and stumping, on cream laid paper
items.description_narrative: This drawing, titled "Male Nude," captures the human form with precision through various graphite pencils, incorporating techniques like erasing and stumping. Created by Gustav Klimt on January 29, 1880, it showcases his early mastery of academic draftsmanship.
items.tags: male nude, drawing, graphite, academic, study, figure drawing, early work, austrian

items.title: Seated Woman from the Front with Hat, Face Hooded
items.cultural_context: Austrian Symbolism, Art Nouveau, Vienna Secession
items.medium: Graphite, with colored pencil, on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Gustav Klimt's "Seated Woman from the Front with Hat, Face Hooded," created in 1910, is a delicate drawing rendered in graphite and colored pencil on ivory wove paper. This work exemplifies the artist's characteristic exploration of the human figure and decorative elements.
items.tags: drawing, figure study, portrait, modern art, early 20th century, Klimt, Austrian art, symbolism

items.title: Paris Street; Rainy Day
items.description_narrative: This painting captures a specific moment at a Parisian intersection on a wet, grey day, depicting well-dressed figures with umbrellas navigating the wide boulevards. Caillebotte employs a striking, almost photographic perspective to illustrate the anonymity and scale of modern urban life.
items.tags: paris, street, rainy, city life, urban, impressionism, realism, modern art

items.title: Hercules and the Lernaean Hydra
items.description_narrative: Gustave Moreau's 'Hercules and the Lernaean Hydra' vividly captures the mythical hero in his epic struggle against the monstrous, multi-headed serpent. This oil painting from 1875–76 emphasizes the dramatic confrontation with a sense of mystical intensity.
items.tags: mythology, symbolism, Hercules, hero, monster, epic, dramatic, oil painting

items.title: Calf's Head and Ox Tongue
items.description_narrative: Gustave Caillebotte presents a stark still life featuring a calf's head and an ox tongue, rendered with unflinching realism. This painting showcases Caillebotte's attention to detail and his distinctive approach to everyday subjects.
items.tags: still life, meat, realism, naturalism, food, detailed

items.title: Alpine Scene
items.description_narrative: Gustave Doré's 'Alpine Scene' captures the majestic and often dramatic vistas of high mountain regions. Painted in 1865, this oil on canvas work exemplifies his skill in rendering natural grandeur and atmospheric depth.
items.tags: alpine, landscape, mountains, romanticism, 19th century, oil painting, french art

items.title: Mère Grégoire
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet's 'Mère Grégoire' presents an unidealized portrait of an ordinary woman, characteristic of the artist's commitment to depicting everyday life. This oil on canvas exemplifies Courbet's pioneering role in the Realist movement, focusing on tangible subjects without romantic embellishment.
items.tags: portrait, realism, 19th century, French art, oil painting, woman, unidealized, naturalism

items.title: The Girl by the Window
items.description_narrative: Edvard Munch's 'The Girl by the Window' from 1893 depicts a solitary figure in an interior space, her back mostly turned to the viewer. Executed in oil on canvas, the work conveys a sense of introspection and quiet observation.
items.tags: portrait, interior, solitude, symbolism, norwegian art, melancholy, expressionism

items.title: The Scream
items.medium: Lithograph in black ink on cream card
items.description_narrative: A lone figure on a bridge clutches its head, expressing a profound sense of anxiety amidst a swirling, fiery landscape. This lithograph captures a powerful moment of existential dread, making visible an internal scream that reverberates through the natural world.
items.tags: expressionism, anxiety, psychological, landscape, print, norwegian, modern

items.title: Two Women on the Shore
items.medium: Woodcut printed from one block (sawn into three sections) in dark blue, green, black and red-brown ink with additions in green crayon on cream Japanese paper
items.description_narrative: This 1898 woodcut by Edvard Munch, titled 'Two Women on the Shore,' features two figures against a coastal backdrop. Munch employed a distinctive technique, printing from a single woodblock sawn into three sections and inked with dark blue, green, black, and red-brown inks, along with green crayon additions.
items.tags: woodcut, printmaking, norwegian art, symbolism, modern art, figure study, coastline

items.title: Consolation
items.medium: Drypoint and open bite in black on cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: Consolation is a drypoint and open bite print created by Edvard Munch in 1894. This artwork, characteristic of Munch's evocative style, utilizes stark contrasts to convey a poignant emotional state.
items.tags: munch, drypoint, printmaking, symbolism, expressionism, melancholy, 19th century, graphic arts

items.title: The Sick Child I
items.medium: Transfer lithograph printed from two stones in pale blue and black ink on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Edvard Munch's "The Sick Child I" is a poignant transfer lithograph, created in 1896 using pale blue and black ink on ivory wove paper. This work delves into themes of illness and vulnerability, reflecting the artist's deeply personal and emotive style through printmaking.
items.tags: illness, childhood, melancholy, lithography, symbolism, expressionism, grief, printmaking

items.title: Madonna
items.medium: Handcolored lithograph in black on mottled gray-blue wove paper (discolored to gray-green), laid down on white wove paper
items.description_narrative: This handcolored lithograph by Edvard Munch, titled 'Madonna', presents a striking and iconic image. Created between 1895 and 1896, it exemplifies the artist's intense exploration of human emotion through printmaking.
items.tags: madonna, figure, lithograph, expressionism, symbolism, emotional, modern

items.title: The Dead Mother and Her Child
items.medium: Etching with open bite and drypoint in black ink on heavyweight cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: This etching by Edvard Munch portrays a poignant scene of a grieving child beside her deceased mother. Through stark lines and a somber composition, Munch powerfully conveys themes of loss and the profound emotional impact of mortality.
items.tags: death, grief, childhood, loss, symbolism, expressionism, psychological, printmaking

items.title: Boys Bathing
items.medium: Color burnished aquatint, inked à la poupée, on buff laid paper
items.description_narrative: This vibrant color burnished aquatint by Edvard Munch depicts a scene of boys bathing, showcasing his mastery of printmaking. Munch employed the à la poupée inking technique to achieve its rich, varied tones and expressive quality.
items.tags: boys, bathing, aquatint, printmaking, symbolism, norwegian art, figural
